detail:
Decisions: Chose a MINOR bump (2.6.0) rather than patch or major — the release adds new tool options (housekeeping archive/repair_entity_scopes), new record fields (rationale_source, warnings_omitted) and changes visible retrieval behavior, which is more than a patch; but no MCP tool was removed or renamed and reason_rejected becoming optional is additive from a client's perspective, so it is not a major; Chose to release before starting benchmark-harness work — the harness installs twining via unpinned `npx -y twining-mcp`, so it resolves to npm latest and literally cannot observe unreleased fixes; releasing unblocks both the field project and any pre/post benchmark comparison
Findings: The benchmark harness's twining conditions install with `npx -y twining-mcp` and NO version pin (src/conditions/twining-*.ts), and environment.twiningMcpVersion is EMPTY in all 15 recorded runs. The 892 pooled sessions spanning Feb-April are therefore version-uncontrolled — they tested whatever was npm latest that day, across a 1.x to 2.x transition. Historical results are directionally usable but are not a clean baseline for pre/post.; warning: the benchmark's decision-documentation scorer (conflict-resolution.ts:415) credits only tool names matching /twining.*decide|twining.*decision/ — twining_record does NOT match despite being the most-called tool (334 calls across the pooled run). twining_decide is full-surface-only and was called ZERO times. So the dimension is structurally a full-surface detector, and its +64 lift for twining-full over baseline is substantially a measurement artifact.; warning: the same scorer's coordination-file fallback pattern /\.twining\/decisions\// misses v2's sqlite layout .twining/records/decisions/. Since v2 defaults new projects to sqlite, this already affects current runs, not just future ones.; Effect decomposition from the pooled run is decisive about where value comes from: orientation (+5.9, 1.2 calls/sess) and recording (+5.9, 1.7 calls/sess) are the ENTIRE measured effect. graph_building, verification, coordination_mgmt, search_retrieval, lifecycle and decision_mgmt all show 0.0 calls and no heavy users. 30 tools were never called once across ~200 sessions.
summary: Preparing the 2.6.0 deep-review release: CHANGELOG written covering 8 fixes, 6 additions, and plugin 1.24.0
